questions.question:
The Pie chart given below shows the distribution of costs of making a water bottle by a company. If the company earns 20% on cost per bottle and the cost of packaging one bottle is Rs. 0.50, then what is the selling price of one bottle?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aab01ef5baff55df9095552247d07386f0e4f97777c83de4efe3ee5bbcea6e15.png]
questions.solution:
Cost of packaging one bottle = Rs. 0.50

⇒ cost of packaging = 5% × cost price of one bottle

⇒ 0.5 = 5% × cost price of one bottle

⇒ cost price of one bottle = 0.5/5% = Rs. 10

Selling price of one bottle = cost price of one bottle × (100 + profit)%

⇒ selling price of one bottle = 10 × 120% = Rs. 12

∴ Selling price of one bottle is Rs. 12

questions.question: A temple has five bells which ring at the intervals of 12, 15, 16, 20 and 25 minutes respectively. If they ring together at midnight, then at what time next will they ring together?
questions.solution:
L.C.M. of 12, 15, 16, 20 and 25

12 = 2 × 2 × 3

15 = 3 × 5

16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2

20 = 2 × 2 × 5

25 = 5 × 5

Hence, L.C.M. = 2⁴ × 3 × 5 × 5 = 1200 minutes = 1200/60 = 20 hours

They will ring together again = 12 AM + 20 hours = 8 PM

∴ They will ring together again at 8 PM.

questions.solution:

Hence, cost price of 1 dozen of potatoes = 200/20 = Rs. 10

Now, selling price of 1 dozen of potatoes = Rs. 9

Rightarrow {{}}Discount \% = frac{{{{cost price}} - {{ selling price}}}}{{{{cost price}}}} times 100 = frac{{1 times 100}}{{10}} = 10\% 

∴ Seller discounted offer is 10%.

questions.question: A cricket team has scored 156 runs in 30 overs. They need to score 275 in 50 overs. What is the average runs per over they need to score in the next 20 overs?
questions.solution:
Cricket team need to run in the next 20 overs = 275 – 156 = 119

Hence, average runs per over they need to score in the next 20 overs = 119/20 = 5.95

∴ The average runs per over they need to score in the next 20 overs is 5.95

questions.question: The simple interest on Rs. x for m years at a rate of r% is equal to the simple interest on Rs. y for n years at the rate of s%, then find x/y.
questions.solution:
Simple interest = PRT/100

⇒ (x × r × m)/100 = (y × s × n)/100

⇒ x × r × m = y × s × n

∴ x/y = ns/mr

questions.question: A rectangular park was redesigned and as a result of which its length increased by 50%. If the area of the park, remained unchanged, then by how much percentage the breadth had been reduced?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Increase in length of park = 50%

Area of the park remain unchanged.

**Concept Used:**

area of park = area of redesigned park.

**Calculation:**

Let length and breadth of the park be l and b

⇒ Length of redesigned park = l × (100 + 50) % = 1.5l

Now,

area of park = area of redesigned park

⇒ l × b = 1.5l × breath

⇒ Breath = b/1.5 = (2/3)b

Hence, reduced breadth = b – (2/3)b = (1/3)b

Reduced breadth in percentage = [(b/3)/b] × 100 = 33.33%

**∴ The breadth had been reduced by 33.33%**

questions.question: A spherical ball of diameter 35 cm rolls 20 times. How much is the distance (in m) covered by it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the spherical ball = 35 cm.

No. of revolutions of the ball = 20 times.

**Concept used:**

distance covered by spherical ball = 2πr × number of revolution.

**Calculation:**

Diameter = 2 × radius

⇒ Radius = 35/2 cm

Now,

⇒ Distance covered by spherical ball = 2 times frac{{22}}{7} times frac{{35}}{2} times 20

⇒ Distance covered by spherical ball = 2200 cm = 22 m (∵ 100 cm = 1 m)

**∴ Distance covered by spherical ball is 22 m.**

An experienced carpenter can complete a woodwork in 8 days. A young carpenter can complete the same work in 12 days. Both work together for 3 days, and then the latter leaves. How may days will be taken by the former to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Let total work = LCM of (8 and 12) = 24 units

Hence, the efficiency of experienced carpenter = 24/8 = 3 units/day

And, the efficiency of young carpenter = 24/12 = 2 units/day

Both work together for 3 days, work done = (3 + 2) × 3 = 15 units

Hence, remaining work = 24 – 15 = 9 units

Now, time taken for remaining work = frac{{Remaining work}}{{Efficiency of experienced carpenter}} 

⇒ time taken for remaining work {{ }} = (9)/({3 )} = 3 days

∴ Former carpenter will complete the remaining work in 3 days.

questions.question: The ratio of boys and girls in a college was 4 : 5. New students admitted and the number of boys went up by 50% and the number of girls went up by 60%. What is the new ratio of boys and girls in the college?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of boys and girls in a college was 4 : 5. New students admitted and the number of boys went up by 50% and the number of girls went up by 60%

**Calculation:**

Let the number of boys and girls initially be 4x and 5x.

Hence, after new students admitted, number of boys = 4x × 150% = 6x

And, number of girls = 5x × 160% = 8x

New ratio of boys and girls = 6x : 8x = 3 : 4

**∴ the correct answer is 3 : 4.**

questions.question: For every Rs. 5 worth of revenue, a retailer earns Rs. 1. If the cost of the goods was Rs. 4800, then how much did he earn?
questions.solution:
Given, Profit = Rs. 1

We know, cost price = revenue – profit

⇒ Cost price = 5 – 1 = Rs. 4

⇒ Profit % = (profit/cost price) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1/4) × 100 = 25%

If, cost price = Rs. 4800

⇒ Profit = cost price × profit%

⇒ Profit = 4800 × 25% = Rs. 1200

∴ Retailer earned Rs. 1200.

questions.question: The length and the breadth of a cuboid are increased by 10% each, whereas the height is reduced by 10%. By how much did the volume change?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Increase in Length and Breadth = 10%

Decrease in Height = 10%

**Formula Used:**

volume of cuboid = length × breadth × height

**Calculation:**

Let the length, breadth and height be 10

⇒ The volume of cuboid = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000

After changing the length of sides, volume of cuboid = (110% × length) × (110% × breadth) × (90% × height)

⇒ The volume of cuboid = 11 × 11 × 9 = 1089

Hence, volume changed = 1089 – 1000 = 89

**∴ volume changed % = (89/1000) × 100 = 8.9 %**

questions.question: 30 dozens of nuts were bought for Rs. 14400. If the nuts are sold in a packet of 5 for Rs. 250, then how much profit is earned?
questions.solution:
Cost price of 30 dozens of nuts = Rs. 14400

⇒ Cost price of one nut = 14400/(30 × 12) = Rs. 40

⇒ Selling price of 5 nuts = Rs. 250

⇒ Selling price of one nut = 250/5 = Rs. 50

Rightarrow {{ }}Profit \% = frac{{selling price - cost price}}{{cost price}} times 100

Rightarrow {{ }}Profit \% = frac{{50 - 40}}{{40}} times 100

Rightarrow {{}}Profit \% = (1)/(4) times 100 = 25\%

⇒ Profit = cost price × profit %

⇒ Profit = 14400 × 25% = Rs. 3600

∴ Total profit is Rs. 3600.

questions.question: A man can row a boat in still water at a speed of 5 m/s. He covers a stretch of 200 m in a river downstream during high and low tides in 10 s and 25 s respectively. What is the ratio of the speed (in m/s) of the water flowing in the river during high and low tides?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of high and low tides be x and y

The speed of boat in high tide (downstream) = x + 5

⇒ Speed = Distance/time

⇒ x + 5 = 200/10

⇒ x + 5 = 20

⇒ x = 15 m/sec

Similarly, y + 5 = 200/25

⇒ y = 3 m/sec

∴ The ratio of the speed of the water flowing in the river during high and low tides = 15 : 3 = 5 : 1

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work alone in 15 and 30 days respectively. In how many days can they together complete the work?
questions.solution:
A and B can complete the work = (d₁ × d₂)/ (d₁ + d₂)

⇒ A and B complete the work = 15 × 30/45 = 10 days

∴ A and B can complete the work in 10 days.

**Alternate method∶**

Suppose the total work = LCM of (15 and 30) = 30 units

Hence, efficiency of A = 30/15 = 2 units/day

And, efficiency of B = 30/30 = 1 unit/day

Now, combined efficiency of A and B = 2 + 1 = 3 units

∴ Time taken to complete work by A and B = 30/3 = 10 days

questions.question: The average weight of a group of eight peoples increased by 2.5 kg when a person weighing 80 kg joined in place of one of the members of the group. Find the weight of the member replaced.
questions.solution:
Average weight of a group of eight peoples increased by 2.5 kg

Hence, Increased weight = 2.5 × 8 = 20 kg

∴ The weight of the replaced member = 80 – 20 = 60 kg
